newsitem.title: USA: Circus says three board members retire.
newsitem.headline: Circus says three board members retire.

text.p: Circus Circus Enterprises Inc said Tuesday three of its directors have retired following the board's adoption of a 70-year-old mandatory retirement age, and they have been replaced by three new members.

The three retiring members are William Pennington, 73, a co-founder and former president, Carl Dodge, 81, former chairman of the Nevada Gaming Commission and Arthur Smith, Jr, 74, former chairman of First Interstate Bank of Nevada.

Replacing the three are Richard Banis, 51, a former president and chief operating officer, Michael McKee, 50, executive vice president of The Irvine Company, and Richard Etter, 57, former chairman of Bank of America-Nevada.
Separately, Kurt Sullivan is resigning as a director to ensure a majority of outside members among the nine-person board. He will remain senior vice president of operations.
